e3087267751432946f63669eb87af1b07a6a21d8: La Planche des Belles Filles is a modestly sized, low-key resort — 3 km of runs for an intimate skiing experience, far from the bustle of the big resorts. This is where you come for calm, authenticity and lift queues that barely exist. La Planche des Belles Filles' reputation as a family resort is well earned: dedicated beginner areas, well-groomed green runs and a friendly atmosphere at the foot of the lifts. It is one of the most reassuring resorts in the Vosges for laying the foundations of skiing with children. The modest altitude of La Planche des Belles Filles — base at 950 m, summit at 1148 m — makes it sensitive to climate variations. January and February remain the safest months for optimal snow cover. Outside this window, checking the snow reports before you set off is strongly advised. With a day lift pass at just €15, La Planche des Belles Filles is one of the most affordable destinations in France. For families on a tight budget, or skiers who want to fit in plenty of days without breaking the bank, it is a sincere and often overlooked choice. In short: La Planche des Belles Filles does not rival the ski giants, and does not pretend to. It is an honest destination, often underrated, that deserves to be (re)discovered.

e35390a4565bd82889615ab2aee73193ca0d8c01: A resort on a human scale, Heiligenblut focuses on friendly welcome and closeness rather than impressive figures. Its 55 km of runs are ideal for a 3–4 day stay, especially with family or for skiers who don't need to constantly change their playground. Heiligenblut's family reputation is well deserved: dedicated beginner areas, a well-run childcare service, well-groomed green runs and a good-natured atmosphere at the foot of the lifts. It's one of the most reassuring resorts in the Northern Alps for learning to ski with children. With a summit at 2902 m and a village at 1301 m, snow reliability at Heiligenblut is generally dependable from January to the end of March. A few exceptionally mild winters can cause tension early in the season, but the situation recovers quickly once serious snowfalls arrive. The budget for a stay at Heiligenblut is clearly high: 60€ for a day lift pass, plus accommodation and mountain restaurants among the most expensive in the Alps. It's the price of excellence, but be aware of it before you go. In short: Heiligenblut lives up to its promises. A Northern Alps resort that will suit most profiles without disappointing.
